steps.reasoning:
The user asks:

"According to Stats Canada, which three categories regarding timber assets in Quebec (by area in hectares) saw the largest raw growth from 1961 to 1962?"

We need stats Canada data for timber assets in Quebec (area in hectares). We need categories of timber assets - likely categories such as "softwood stands above 1 ha", etc. From 1961 to 1962 raw growth. So difference between 1962 and 1961 for each category, then the top three with largest raw growth.

It's specialized. Need up-to-date sources. Search web.

There is a long history of hunting and trapping activities in Canada, though a decline in participation has been  
documented in recent decades.74 Waterfowl primarily use wetland and grassland habitat in coastal areas, on the  
Prairies and the boreal forest.75 Environment and Climate Change Canada’s Waterfowl Harvest Survey indicates that  
an estimated 1,153,000 ducks, 1,014,900 geese and 54,000 non-waterfowl birds were harvested in 2015.76 In 2009,  
730,900 pelts from muskrat, beaver, martens, ermines, foxes, bears and other fur-bearing animals were harvested,  
with a total reported value of $14.8 million.77 Hunting licenses for big game, for example deer, moose, bear, elk and  
caribou among other animals, are issued by the provinces and territories.
Biodiversity and ecosystem services  
Biodiversity plays an important role in supporting human well-being since it affects the productivity and resilience of  
ecosystems that provide us with ecosystem services. For example, trees provide carbon storage services, mitigating  
climate change; insects, birds, bats and rodents help disperse seeds, regenerating forests; birds and bats eat insects,  
controlling pest populations; plants help reduce water runoff and reduce soil erosion.78 Sustainable management of  
forest ecosystems considers the benefits of these services in addition to those provided by the production of timber  
and other forest products.

Biodiversity and ecosystem services  
Biodiversity plays an important role in supporting human well-being since it affects the productivity and resilience of  
ecosystems that provide us with ecosystem services. For example, trees provide carbon storage services, mitigating  
climate change; insects, birds, bats and rodents help disperse seeds, regenerating forests; birds and bats eat insects,  
controlling pest populations; plants help reduce water runoff and reduce soil erosion.78 Sustainable management of  
forest ecosystems considers the benefits of these services in addition to those provided by the production of timber  
and other forest products.

steps.reasoning:
The question: "According to Stats Canada, which three categories regarding timber assets in Quebec (by area in hectares) saw the largest raw growth from 1961 to 1962?" So need to look at Timber assets (area) dataset for Quebec, 1961 and 1962 values for various categories. Then compute raw growth (difference) and pick top 3 categories with largest increase.

The dataset includes categories: "Timber assets (area)" (overall), "non reserved accessible opening stock", "fire", "mortality", "harvest", "regeneration", etc. We need to compute raw growth for each category.

We need the values for Quebec in 1961 and 1962. The dataset appears as a web page with table; easier to download CSV maybe via dataset link (38100106-eng.csv) or similar. Let's fetch the CSV.

Use web_search or web_fetch? We have not set a web_fetch tool but we can use web_download via the link. However the function available is web_search only. But we can get more details. Maybe we can use web_search to get specific numeric values.

Title: Historical, 1901-1961 = Chronologie, 1901-1961. : Canada. Dominion Bureau of Statistics = Bureau fédéral de la statistique. : Free Download, Borrow, and Streaming : Internet Archive
Chunks: 0,1,2,3
INTRODUCTION
The historical table in this report provides an account of population growth in Canada during the present century.This table presents population counts from earlier censuses not only for provinces,counties and census divisions,but also at the level of cities,towns,villages,municipalities,townships,and other types of municipal and census sub divisions.
For all provinces except Newfoundland and British Columbia,population counts are shown back to the 1901 Census.In the case of Newfoundland,they include only the censuses taken since New foundland became a province of Canada in 1949,(viz.,1951,1956,and 1961).Table 6 of Volume I of the 1951 Census provides‘‘tie-in’’data with the 1945 Census taken by the Government of New foundland.
For the province of British Columbia,it is possible to show population counts for the census subdivisions established in this province for the 1931 Census,only back to 1921.Counts from 1901 to the present census,however,are shown for the 10 census divisions at the end of the British Columbia portion of this report,and for the incor porated cities and villages(1901-51)at Table 9 of Volume I of the 1951 Census.
Population counts for municipal subdivisions refer to their areas as incorporated at any given census date.Where boundary changes have occurred which affect the comparability of the figures from one census to another,these are explained wherever possible by means of footnotes at the end of the table.The only exception to the foregoing is in the case of the rural municipalities(i.e.,municipal dis tricts,improvement districts,etc.)of Alberta.For pur poses of comparison,population counts for all years previous to 1956 are based on the areas existing at the date of the 1956 Census.This was made neces sary due to the complete reorganizations of these mu nicipal subdivisions in Alberta between 1941 and 1956.

Certain minor changes in the county boundaries of Quebec and Ontario which have occurred in recent years have not been followed in this report,for a similar reason.that it would be impossible to make comparisons with earlier censuses.These differ ences are explained at the conclusion of the sections of this report dealing with Quebec and Ontario.Further,in the case of Alberta and Manitoba,the municipal subdivisions are arranged within the boundaries of the new census divisions as revised prior to the 1956 and 1961 Censuses,respectively.
Population counts at the county and municipal subdivision level prior to 1901 are available for some of the provinces in volumes of earlier cen suses.For example,figures from 1871 to 1951 inclusive are shown for Prince Edward Island,Nova Scotia,New Brunswick,Quebec,Ontario,and Manitoba at Table 6 of Volume I of the 1951 Census.
Note:This report comprises Table 6 of Volume I(Part 1)of the 1961 Census.To combine this table in its correct sequence with others in the same series,it should be placed following Table 5(Electoral districts and census subdivisions)which appeared in Report No.1.1—1,and ahead of Table 7(Counties and census subdivisions)which ap peared in Reports 1.1—2 to 1.1—5 inclusive.
606 1-527
Le tableau chronologique du présent rapport donne la statistique de l’accroissement de la population au Canada depuis le début du siècle.Il récapitule les chiffres de la population des recensements antérieurs non seulement pour les provinces,comtés et divisions de recensement mais aussi pour les cités,villes,vil lages,municipalités,cantons ou townships et autres ca tégories de subdivisions municipales et de recensement.

Dans le cas de toutes les provinces,sauf Terre Neuve et la Colombie-Britannique,les chiffres de la population remontent au recensement de 1901.Dans celui de Terre-Neuve,la statistique n’indique que les recensements effectués depuis que Terre-Neuve est devenue province du Canada en 1949(ceux de 1951,1956 et 1961).Le tableau 6,du Volume I du recensement de 1951 donne les chiffres correspondants du recensement de 1945 effectué par le gouvernement de Terre-Neuve.
En Colombie-Britannique,il n’est possible d’indi quer le chiffre de la population des subdivisions de recensement établies dans cette province pour le re censement de 1931,qu’à compter de 1921.Cependant,pour les 10 divisions de recensement,on donne le chiffre de la population depuis 1901 jusqu’au dernier recensement à la fin de la section du présent rapport qui a trait à la Colombie-Britannique;la population des cités et villages constitués(1901-1951)paraît au tableau 9 du Volume I du recensement de 1951.
La population des subdivisions municipales res pecte les limites établies à un recensement donné.Lorsqu’il est survenu des changements de limites qui détruisent la comparabilité des données,on les signale 14 où c’est possible au moyen de renvois à la fin du tableau.La seule exception à ce qui précède concerne les municipalités rurales(i.e.,districts municipaux,districts d’amélioration,etc.)de l'Alberta.Pour les fins de comparaison,le chiffre de la population de toutes les années antérieures à 1956 se fonde sur les limites existantes au recensement de 1956.Il a fallu en agir ainsi à cause du remaniement complet de ces subdivisions municipales en Alberta entre 1941 et 1956.

Certains changements de peu d'importance sont survenus ces dernières années dans les limites de comtés du Québec et de l'Ontario;mais le présent rapport n’en tient pas compte parce qu'il serait alors impossible d’établir des comparaisons avec les recen sements antérieurs.Ces différences sont expliquées à la fin des sections du présent rapport qui traitent du Québec et de l'Ontario.En outre,dans le cas de l'Alberta et du Manitoba,les subdivisions municipales sont disposées à l’intérieur des limites des nouvelles divisions de recensement revisées,respectivement,avant les recensements de 1956 et de 1961.
Les chiffres de la population avant 1901 par comté et subdivision municipale existent pour certaines pro vinces dans les volumes des recensements antérieurs.Par exemple,le tableau 6 du Volume I du recensement de 1951 donne les chiffres de 1871 à 1951 inclus pour l’Île-du-Prince-Édouard,la Nouvelle-Écosse,le Nou veau-Brunswick,le Québec,l'Ontario et le Manitoba.
Nota:Le présent rapport constitue le tableau 6 du Volume I(Partie 1)du recensement de 1961.Pour situer ce tableau au bon endroit dans la série,il faut le placer après le tableau 5(districts électoraux et subdivisions de recensement)qui a paru dans le Rapport 1.1—1,et avant le tableau 7(comtés et sub divisions de recensement)qui a paru dans les Rapports 1.1—2 à 1.1—5 inclus.

The **1961 Canadian census** was a detailed enumeration of the Canadian population. Census day was June 16, 1961. On that day, Statistics Canada attempted to count every person in Canada. The total population count of Canada was 18,238,247. This was a 13.4% increase over the 1956 census of 16,080,791.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1961_Canadian_census#cite_note-1)
The previous census was the 1956 census and the following census was the 1966 census. This was the first census since 1901 in which all then-admitted provinces recorded a population of at least 100,000, and the last in which Saskatchewan had a larger population than neighbouring Manitoba.

INTRODUCTION
The historical table in this report provides an account of population growth in Canada during the present century.This table presents population counts from earlier censuses not only for provinces,counties and census divisions,but also at the level of cities,towns,villages,municipalities,townships,and other types of municipal and census sub divisions.
For all provinces except Newfoundland and British Columbia,population counts are shown back to the 1901 Census.In the case of Newfoundland,they include only the censuses taken since New foundland became a province of Canada in 1949,(viz.,1951,1956,and 1961).Table 6 of Volume I of the 1951 Census provides‘‘tie-in’’data with the 1945 Census taken by the Government of New foundland.
For the province of British Columbia,it is possible to show population counts for the census subdivisions established in this province for the 1931 Census,only back to 1921.Counts from 1901 to the present census,however,are shown for the 10 census divisions at the end of the British Columbia portion of this report,and for the incor porated cities and villages(1901-51)at Table 9 of Volume I of the 1951 Census.
Population counts for municipal subdivisions refer to their areas as incorporated at any given census date.Where boundary changes have occurred which affect the comparability of the figures from one census to another,these are explained wherever possible by means of footnotes at the end of the table.The only exception to the foregoing is in the case of the rural municipalities(i.e.,municipal dis tricts,improvement districts,etc.)of Alberta.For pur poses of comparison,population counts for all years previous to 1956 are based on the areas existing at the date of the 1956 Census.This was made neces sary due to the complete reorganizations of these mu nicipal subdivisions in Alberta between 1941 and 1956.

Certain minor changes in the county boundaries of Quebec and Ontario which have occurred in recent years have not been followed in this report,for a similar reason.that it would be impossible to make comparisons with earlier censuses.These differ ences are explained at the conclusion of the sections of this report dealing with Quebec and Ontario.Further,in the case of Alberta and Manitoba,the municipal subdivisions are arranged within the boundaries of the new census divisions as revised prior to the 1956 and 1961 Censuses,respectively.
Population counts at the county and municipal subdivision level prior to 1901 are available for some of the provinces in volumes of earlier cen suses.For example,figures from 1871 to 1951 inclusive are shown for Prince Edward Island,Nova Scotia,New Brunswick,Quebec,Ontario,and Manitoba at Table 6 of Volume I of the 1951 Census.
Note:This report comprises Table 6 of Volume I(Part 1)of the 1961 Census.To combine this table in its correct sequence with others in the same series,it should be placed following Table 5(Electoral districts and census subdivisions)which appeared in Report No.1.1—1,and ahead of Table 7(Counties and census subdivisions)which ap peared in Reports 1.1—2 to 1.1—5 inclusive.

Le tableau chronologique du présent rapport donne la statistique de l’accroissement de la population au Canada depuis le début du siècle.Il récapitule les chiffres de la population des recensements antérieurs non seulement pour les provinces,comtés et divisions de recensement mais aussi pour les cités,villes,vil lages,municipalités,cantons ou townships et autres ca tégories de subdivisions municipales et de recensement.

Dans le cas de toutes les provinces,sauf Terre Neuve et la Colombie-Britannique,les chiffres de la population remontent au recensement de 1901.Dans celui de Terre-Neuve,la statistique n’indique que les recensements effectués depuis que Terre-Neuve est devenue province du Canada en 1949(ceux de 1951,1956 et 1961).Le tableau 6,du Volume I du recensement de 1951 donne les chiffres correspondants du recensement de 1945 effectué par le gouvernement de Terre-Neuve.
En Colombie-Britannique,il n’est possible d’indi quer le chiffre de la population des subdivisions de recensement établies dans cette province pour le re censement de 1931,qu’à compter de 1921.Cependant,pour les 10 divisions de recensement,on donne le chiffre de la population depuis 1901 jusqu’au dernier recensement à la fin de la section du présent rapport qui a trait à la Colombie-Britannique;la population des cités et villages constitués(1901-1951)paraît au tableau 9 du Volume I du recensement de 1951.
La population des subdivisions municipales res pecte les limites établies à un recensement donné.Lorsqu’il est survenu des changements de limites qui détruisent la comparabilité des données,on les signale 14 où c’est possible au moyen de renvois à la fin du tableau.La seule exception à ce qui précède concerne les municipalités rurales(i.e.,districts municipaux,districts d’amélioration,etc.)de l'Alberta.Pour les fins de comparaison,le chiffre de la population de toutes les années antérieures à 1956 se fonde sur les limites existantes au recensement de 1956.Il a fallu en agir ainsi à cause du remaniement complet de ces subdivisions municipales en Alberta entre 1941 et 1956.

Certains changements de peu d'importance sont survenus ces dernières années dans les limites de comtés du Québec et de l'Ontario;mais le présent rapport n’en tient pas compte parce qu'il serait alors impossible d’établir des comparaisons avec les recen sements antérieurs.Ces différences sont expliquées à la fin des sections du présent rapport qui traitent du Québec et de l'Ontario.En outre,dans le cas de l'Alberta et du Manitoba,les subdivisions municipales sont disposées à l’intérieur des limites des nouvelles divisions de recensement revisées,respectivement,avant les recensements de 1956 et de 1961.
Les chiffres de la population avant 1901 par comté et subdivision municipale existent pour certaines pro vinces dans les volumes des recensements antérieurs.Par exemple,le tableau 6 du Volume I du recensement de 1951 donne les chiffres de 1871 à 1951 inclus pour l’Île-du-Prince-Édouard,la Nouvelle-Écosse,le Nou veau-Brunswick,le Québec,l'Ontario et le Manitoba.
Nota:Le présent rapport constitue le tableau 6 du Volume I(Partie 1)du recensement de 1961.Pour situer ce tableau au bon endroit dans la série,il faut le placer après le tableau 5(districts électoraux et subdivisions de recensement)qui a paru dans le Rapport 1.1—1,et avant le tableau 7(comtés et sub divisions de recensement)qui a paru dans les Rapports 1.1—2 à 1.1—5 inclus.

The **1961 Canadian census** was a detailed enumeration of the Canadian population. Census day was June 16, 1961. On that day, Statistics Canada attempted to count every person in Canada. The total population count of Canada was 18,238,247. This was a 13.4% increase over the 1956 census of 16,080,791.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1961_Canadian_census#cite_note-1)
The previous census was the 1956 census and the following census was the 1966 census. This was the first census since 1901 in which all then-admitted provinces recorded a population of at least 100,000, and the last in which Saskatchewan had a larger population than neighbouring Manitoba.

The **1961 Canadian census** was a detailed enumeration of the Canadian population. Census day was June 16, 1961. On that day, Statistics Canada attempted to count every person in Canada. The total population count of Canada was 18,238,247. This was a 13.4% increase over the 1956 census of 16,080,791.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1961_Canadian_census#cite_note-1)
The previous census was the 1956 census and the following census was the 1966 census. This was the first census since 1901 in which all then-admitted provinces recorded a population of at least 100,000, and the last in which Saskatchewan had a larger population than neighbouring Manitoba.

A different definition for the Northwest Territories disregards areas not included within the Mackenzie River Electoral District. If such areas were excluded, the Northwest Territories had 14,895 people in 1961 and 12,492 people in 1956.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1961_Canadian_census#cite_note-2) Under this definition, the Northwest Territories saw an increase of 2,403 people, or 19.2%.

Source: https://people.sc.fsu.edu/~jburkardt/data/csv/csv.html
Title: CSV Files
Chunks: 0,1,2,3,4,5
* * *
**CSV** is a data directory which contains examples of CSV files, a flat file format describing values in a table.
Each record consists of M values, separated by commas. However, the last value is not followed by a comma.
Double quotes are used as escape characters. A string with a comma can be delimited by double quotes so that that comma is not misinterpreted as a field separator.
To de-escape a double quote, that is, to use it literally, use two double quotes.
A final, unmatched, double quote on a line indicates that that line is to be continued on the next line.
In some cases, a CSV file includes an initial line of headers.

### Licensing:
The computer code and data files described and made available on this web page are distributed under the GNU LGPL license.

### Sample Files:
*   addresses.csv, an example file with 6 records. There are 6 fields.   
*   airtravel.csv, Monthly transatlantic airtravel, in thousands of passengers, for 1958-1960. There are 4 fields, "Month", "1958", "1959" and "1960" and 12 records, "JAN" through "DEC". There is also an initial header line.   
*   biostats.csv, biometric statistics for a group of office workers. There are 18 records, recording Name, Sex, Age, Height, Weight There is an initial header line.   
*   cities.csv, an example file with 128 records. There are 10 fields.   
*   crash_catalonia.csv, number of car crashes in Catalonia from 2000 to 2011, by day of week. There are 7 records, with two values each. There is also an initial header line.   
*   deniro.csv, Rotten Tomato ratings of movies with Robert De Niro. There are 87 records. Each record has Year, Rating, Titlte. There is also an initial header line.   
*   example.csv, an example file with 1 record. There are 78 values per record. There is also an initial header line.   
*   ford_escort.csv, used Ford Escorts for sale. There are 23 records of year, mileage and price. There is also an initial header line.   
*   faithful.csv, Old Faithful geyser: index, time between eruptions, and length of eruption. 272 records, each with three values. There is also an initial header line.   
*   freshman_kgs.csv, Sex, September weight (kgs), April weight (kgs), September BMI, April BMI, for 67 college freshmen. There is also an initial header line.   
*   freshman_lbs.csv, Sex, September weight (lbs), April weight (lbs), September BMI, April BMI, for 67 college freshmen. There is also an initial header line.   

### Sample Files:
*   grades.csv, an example file with 16 records and 9 fields: First name, Last Name, SSN, Test1, Test2, Test3, Test4, Final, Grade. There is also an initial header line.   
*   homes.csv, Home sale statistics. Fifty home sales, with selling price, asking price, living space, rooms, bedrooms, bathrooms, age, acreage, taxes. There is also an initial header line.   
*   hooke.csv, Hooke's Law demo. A spring experiment is carried out twice. Spring 1 and spring 2 are loaded with 0, 1, 2, ..., 9 equal weights and their lengths are measured. Each record contains the index, weight, spring 1 length and spring 2 length. There is also an initial header line.   
*   hurricanes.csv, hurricane and tropical storm counts for 2005-2015. Each record includes 13 values: month, historical average, counts for 2005 through 2015. Eight records are stored, for months "May" through "Dec". There is also an initial header line.   
*   hw_200.csv, height and weight for 200 individuals Each record includes 3 values: index, height (inches), weight (pounds). There is also an initial header line.   
*   hw_25000.csv, height and weight for 25000 individuals Each record includes 3 values: index, height (inches), weight (pounds). There is also an initial header line.   
*   lead_shot.csv, For each grade of lead shot, a record lists the grade name, the weight in ounces, weight in grams, diameter in inches, diameter in millimeters, and the number of pellets per ounce. There are 25 records. There is also an initial header line.   
*   letter_frequency.csv, In a large text, the frequency and percentage frequency of each of the 26 letters of the alphabet was determined. There are 26 records, each with three values. There is also an initial header line.   

### Sample Files:
*   mlb_players.csv, Major League Baseball Players: Name, Team, Position, height (inches), weight (pounds), age (years). 1034 records, each with six values. There is also an initial header line.   
*   mlb_teams_2012.csv, Major League Baseball 2012 Season: Team, Payroll(millions), Wins. 30 records, each with 3 values. There is also an initial header line.   
*   news_decline.csv, average nightly viewship for 6 TV news magazines for 2009-2011. Each record includes 4 values: show name, 2009, 2010, 2011. Six records are stored, for "60 Minutes", "48 Hours Mystery", "20/20", "Nightline", "Dateline Friday", and "Dateline Sunday". There is also an initial header line.   
*   nile.csv, Nile flood data; 570 records, each with 2 values: year index, maximum height of Nile flood. There is also an initial header line.   
*   oscar_age_female.csv, age of female Oscar winners; 89 records: index, age, name, movie. There is also an initial header line.   
*   oscar_age_male.csv, age of male Oscar winners; 89 records: index, age, name, movie. There is also an initial header line.   
*   snakes_count_10.csv, game length for one-player version of Snakes and Ladders, 10 records, each with 2 values: Game Index, Game Length. There is also an initial header line.   
*   snakes_count_100.csv, game length for one-player version of Snakes and Ladders, 100 records, each with 2 values: Game Index, Game Length. There is also an initial header line.   
*   snakes_count_1000.csv, game length for one-player version of Snakes and Ladders, 1000 records, each with 2 values: Game Index, Game Length. There is also an initial header line.   

### Sample Files:
*   snakes_count_10000.csv, game length for one-player version of Snakes and Ladders, 10000 records, each with 2 values: Game Index, Game Length. There is also an initial header line.   
*   tally_cab.csv, Tallahassee Cab Fares, 8 records, each with 2 values: Distance(miles), Fare($). There is also an initial header line.   
*   taxables.csv, Taxable items, 10 records: index, item name, price, tax, price plus tax. There is also an initial header line.   
*   trees.csv, Tree measurements, 31 records: index, circumference (in), height (ft), volume (ft^3). There is also an initial header line.   
*   zillow.csv, Tallahassee Housing Prices as reported by Zillow, 20 records: Index, Square footage, beds, baths, zip code, year, list price. There is also an initial header line.
You can go up one level to the DATA page.

Title: What's a CSV file?
Chunks: 0
A CSV (comma-separated values) file is a plain text file that stores tabular data, such as numbers and text. Each line in the file represents one data record, and each record consists of the same number of fields separated by commas. For example, a CSV file might contain a list of customers with their names, email addresses, and phone numbers.
Here’s an example of the content in a CSV file:
Copy
Content in a CSV file
`Name,Email Address,Phone NumberJohn Doe,johndoe@example.com,123-456-7890Jane Smith,janesmith@example.com,987-654-3210`
Microsoft Excel is a spreadsheet program that can be used to open, edit, and create CSV files. When you open a CSV file in Excel, the data is automatically formatted into a table with rows and columns. You can then use Excel features to analyze and manipulate the data.
The image below shows the difference between what a CSV files looks like in Excel, and what a CSV file looks like when opened with a text editor.

2.   The same Intacct CSV file opened in a text editor.

Topic updated on August 03, 2026
Downloading data from the Management Portal to a CSV file provides the flexibility to generate your own customized reports from raw data. This section explains importing the CSV file to Microsoft Excel while preserving data types and number formats. In some spreadsheet applications, including Excel, opening the CSV file may default to displaying longer numbers in scientific notation format (for example, _3.42805E+17_). Follow the steps below to prevent this formatting.

# Importing CSV files to Microsoft Excel
1.   In the Management Portal, navigate to the screen containing the data you want to export.  
2.   Do one of the following:  
    1.   To download all the objects, click **Download CSV**.  
    2.   To download the objects listed in a page, click page select and click **Download CSV**.  
    3.   To only download certain objects, select the objects you want to Download and then click **Download CSV**.
The CSV file is generated and is downloaded.
3.   Open a _Blank workbook_ in Microsoft Excel.  
4.   Click on the **Data** menu.  
5.   Click on the **From Text/CSV**.  
6.   Choose the downloaded CSV file.  
7.   Click **Import**.  
8.   Verify if the following options are chosen  
    1.   File Origin: _1200: Unicode_.  
    2.   Delimiter: _Comma_.



9.   Verify the sample layout.  
10.   Click **Load**.

Topic updated on August 03, 2026
Downloading data from the Management Portal to a CSV file provides the flexibility to generate your own customized reports from raw data. This section explains importing the CSV file to Microsoft Excel while preserving data types and number formats. In some spreadsheet applications, including Excel, opening the CSV file may default to displaying longer numbers in scientific notation format (for example, _3.42805E+17_). Follow the steps below to prevent this formatting.
texts.2:
# Importing CSV files to Microsoft Excel
1.   In the Management Portal, navigate to the screen containing the data you want to export.  
2.   Do one of the following:  
    1.   To download all the objects, click **Download CSV**.  
    2.   To download the objects listed in a page, click page select and click **Download CSV**.  
    3.   To only download certain objects, select the objects you want to Download and then click **Download CSV**.
The CSV file is generated and is downloaded.
3.   Open a _Blank workbook_ in Microsoft Excel.  
4.   Click on the **Data** menu.  
5.   Click on the **From Text/CSV**.  
6.   Choose the downloaded CSV file.  
7.   Click **Import**.  
8.   Verify if the following options are chosen  
    1.   File Origin: _1200: Unicode_.  
    2.   Delimiter: _Comma_.



9.   Verify the sample layout.  
10.   Click **Load**.

Title: What's a CSV file?
Chunks: 0
A CSV (comma-separated values) file is a plain text file that stores tabular data, such as numbers and text. Each line in the file represents one data record, and each record consists of the same number of fields separated by commas. For example, a CSV file might contain a list of customers with their names, email addresses, and phone numbers.
Here’s an example of the content in a CSV file:
Copy
Content in a CSV file
`Name,Email Address,Phone NumberJohn Doe,johndoe@example.com,123-456-7890Jane Smith,janesmith@example.com,987-654-3210`
Microsoft Excel is a spreadsheet program that can be used to open, edit, and create CSV files. When you open a CSV file in Excel, the data is automatically formatted into a table with rows and columns. You can then use Excel features to analyze and manipulate the data.
The image below shows the difference between what a CSV files looks like in Excel, and what a CSV file looks like when opened with a text editor.
1.   An Intacct CSV file opened in Excel.

2.   The same Intacct CSV file opened in a text editor.
The extra commas shown in this image are present because there are blank fields in the file. A comma in a CSV file represents a blank cell in Excel.

Source: https://people.sc.fsu.edu/~jburkardt/data/csv/csv.html
Title: CSV Files
Chunks: 0,1,2,3,4,5
* * *
**CSV** is a data directory which contains examples of CSV files, a flat file format describing values in a table.
Each record consists of M values, separated by commas. However, the last value is not followed by a comma.
Double quotes are used as escape characters. A string with a comma can be delimited by double quotes so that that comma is not misinterpreted as a field separator.
To de-escape a double quote, that is, to use it literally, use two double quotes.
A final, unmatched, double quote on a line indicates that that line is to be continued on the next line.
In some cases, a CSV file includes an initial line of headers.

### Sample Files:
*   addresses.csv, an example file with 6 records. There are 6 fields.   
*   airtravel.csv, Monthly transatlantic airtravel, in thousands of passengers, for 1958-1960. There are 4 fields, "Month", "1958", "1959" and "1960" and 12 records, "JAN" through "DEC". There is also an initial header line.   
*   biostats.csv, biometric statistics for a group of office workers. There are 18 records, recording Name, Sex, Age, Height, Weight There is an initial header line.   
*   cities.csv, an example file with 128 records. There are 10 fields.   
*   crash_catalonia.csv, number of car crashes in Catalonia from 2000 to 2011, by day of week. There are 7 records, with two values each. There is also an initial header line.   
*   deniro.csv, Rotten Tomato ratings of movies with Robert De Niro. There are 87 records. Each record has Year, Rating, Titlte. There is also an initial header line.   
*   example.csv, an example file with 1 record. There are 78 values per record. There is also an initial header line.   
*   ford_escort.csv, used Ford Escorts for sale. There are 23 records of year, mileage and price. There is also an initial header line.   
*   faithful.csv, Old Faithful geyser: index, time between eruptions, and length of eruption. 272 records, each with three values. There is also an initial header line.   
*   freshman_kgs.csv, Sex, September weight (kgs), April weight (kgs), September BMI, April BMI, for 67 college freshmen. There is also an initial header line.   
*   freshman_lbs.csv, Sex, September weight (lbs), April weight (lbs), September BMI, April BMI, for 67 college freshmen. There is also an initial header line.   

### Sample Files:
*   grades.csv, an example file with 16 records and 9 fields: First name, Last Name, SSN, Test1, Test2, Test3, Test4, Final, Grade. There is also an initial header line.   
*   homes.csv, Home sale statistics. Fifty home sales, with selling price, asking price, living space, rooms, bedrooms, bathrooms, age, acreage, taxes. There is also an initial header line.   
*   hooke.csv, Hooke's Law demo. A spring experiment is carried out twice. Spring 1 and spring 2 are loaded with 0, 1, 2, ..., 9 equal weights and their lengths are measured. Each record contains the index, weight, spring 1 length and spring 2 length. There is also an initial header line.   
*   hurricanes.csv, hurricane and tropical storm counts for 2005-2015. Each record includes 13 values: month, historical average, counts for 2005 through 2015. Eight records are stored, for months "May" through "Dec". There is also an initial header line.   
*   hw_200.csv, height and weight for 200 individuals Each record includes 3 values: index, height (inches), weight (pounds). There is also an initial header line.   
*   hw_25000.csv, height and weight for 25000 individuals Each record includes 3 values: index, height (inches), weight (pounds). There is also an initial header line.   
*   lead_shot.csv, For each grade of lead shot, a record lists the grade name, the weight in ounces, weight in grams, diameter in inches, diameter in millimeters, and the number of pellets per ounce. There are 25 records. There is also an initial header line.

*   mlb_teams_2012.csv, Major League Baseball 2012 Season: Team, Payroll(millions), Wins. 30 records, each with 3 values. There is also an initial header line.   
*   news_decline.csv, average nightly viewship for 6 TV news magazines for 2009-2011. Each record includes 4 values: show name, 2009, 2010, 2011. Six records are stored, for "60 Minutes", "48 Hours Mystery", "20/20", "Nightline", "Dateline Friday", and "Dateline Sunday". There is also an initial header line.   
*   nile.csv, Nile flood data; 570 records, each with 2 values: year index, maximum height of Nile flood. There is also an initial header line.   
*   oscar_age_female.csv, age of female Oscar winners; 89 records: index, age, name, movie. There is also an initial header line.   
*   oscar_age_male.csv, age of male Oscar winners; 89 records: index, age, name, movie. There is also an initial header line.

*   snakes_count_100.csv, game length for one-player version of Snakes and Ladders, 100 records, each with 2 values: Game Index, Game Length. There is also an initial header line.   
*   snakes_count_1000.csv, game length for one-player version of Snakes and Ladders, 1000 records, each with 2 values: Game Index, Game Length. There is also an initial header line.   

### Sample Files:
*   snakes_count_10000.csv, game length for one-player version of Snakes and Ladders, 10000 records, each with 2 values: Game Index, Game Length. There is also an initial header line.   
*   tally_cab.csv, Tallahassee Cab Fares, 8 records, each with 2 values: Distance(miles), Fare($). There is also an initial header line.

steps.text:
We need to answer: "According to Stats Canada, which three categories regarding timber assets in Quebec (by area in hectares) saw the largest raw growth from 1961 to 1962?" So we need to identify categories of timber assets in Quebec with the largest increase in area (ha) between 1961 and 1962.

The dataset 38100106 covers timber assets (area) includes categories: Timber assets (area), nonreserved accessible opening stock, fire, mortality, harvest, regeneration, roads, nonreserved accessible closing stock, nonstocked accessible closing stock. For Quebec, values for each category for 1961 and 1962. The raw growth = difference between 1961 and 1962. Find the three categories with greatest increase.

We can download CSV maybe. But here we have the dataset ZIPs. Maybe I can fetch CSV file? But web_search returns the URL but not content. We might need to fetch file content via web_fetch? There's no web_fetch tool, but we can perhaps request the CSV via HTTP GET. The environment might not allow arbitrary downloads. I can use web_search again with "38100106-eng.zip" but needed to download. Possibly we can view the downloaded file via link? The open can show maybe small text? The CSV might be large; but maybe the open can read it as text. We can try to fetch with web_search pass to open first line? Maybe we can use web_search with query and open results. The link "https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/tbl/csv/38100106-eng.zip" might be accessible. We can try to open the URL with the function? There's no function other than web_search. web_search returns results including snippet, but not file content. Might open it but the snippet may not show. Maybe we can open using HTTP GET with web_search? Not sure.

Alternatively, dataset might be available as CSV accessible via download for each series. But maybe easier: the dataset includes Quebec values for each category. We can manually find from the source data displayed maybe on the StatCan page. But page earlier didn't show the table. We can maybe use Data: maybe the "Dashboard" where you can choose Quebec. But the raw data not pre-rendered.

We could extract from the 'Archived' content that had earlier variations? The page earlier showing 'forest area' maybe not.

We can try to get the dataset via the link to the table maybe accessible via API? Eg https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/t1/tbl1/en/tv.action?pid=3810010601 Not giving table data directly. But maybe we can request via statcan's API: but time.

We can approximate by reasoning: In Quebec, categories likely include: 'nonreserved accessible opening stock', 'harvest', 'fire', 'mortality', 'regeneration', 'roads', 'nonreserved accessible closing stock', 'nonstocked accessible closing stock'. Which of these grew most between 1961 and 1962? We need raw growth from 1961 to 1962.

We need value for Quebec in 1961 and 1962.

We can search for 'Quebec 1961 timber assets area' within the dataset? Search for 'Quebec 1961 1962 timber assets' maybe find.

Search: "Quebec 1961 1962 timber assets area 38100106"
